reading.body:
H.R. 7110 is a one-party bill: Summer Lee sponsors it and all sixteen cosponsors are Democrats.

The recorded support is entirely from one caucus, which tells you the bill's near-term path is a statement of position rather than a negotiated compromise. The issues tagged from its own text are bias and civil rights, so the measure is aimed at how algorithmic systems treat people, not at how much compute they consume or where the power for it comes from.

The lobbying count is the sharper fact. Zero filings for 2025 or later name this bill, which means no outside interest has yet registered it as an issue in their advocacy. That is not the same as no interest. A filing that names a bill shows only that the bill came up, not what anyone wanted done about it, and the absence of filings may reflect a bill that is early, low-profile, or simply not yet worth lobbying against.

What the data does not cover: the bill's text, its committee stage, any vote, and any position taken by the cosponsors beyond signing on. The latest status date is 2026-01-15, and everything here is a snapshot of sponsorship and lobbying records, not of what the bill would do to data centers, grid interconnection, or the buildout that AI scaling depends on.
